drivers.name: BirdDog NDI Encoder/Decoder
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders via REST API. Select NDI sources on decoders, monitor input/output status, reboot, and refresh source lists.

help.overview:
Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders — Mini, Flex, 4K HDMI, 4K SDI, Studio NDI, PLAY, Quad, and similar models.

For decoders: select which NDI source to display, cycle through available sources, and monitor the active source.

For encoders: monitor input status and NDI source name.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the device's IP address (find it via BirdDog Central or your network's DHCP table).
2. Default port is 8080.
3. No authentication is required.
4. For decoders, use 'select_source' with the full NDI source name (e.g., 'BIRDDOG-P200 (Camera)').
5. Use 'refresh_sources' to update the available source list.

drivers.name: Cisco Webex Codec / Room Series (xAPI)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Cisco Webex video-conferencing endpoints (Codec Pro / Plus / EQ, Room Bar, Room Kit family, Room 55/70 family, Board Pro, Desk family) via the RoomOS xAPI over HTTPS. Standby, volume, mute, dial / hangup, DND, presentation, camera presets, on-screen messaging, reboot. Polling-based — HttpFeedback push deferred until the platform's inbound-listener primitive lands.

help.overview: Cisco Webex video-conferencing endpoints — the Codec Pro / Plus, Room Kit family, Room 55 / 70 series, Board Pro, and Desk Pro — all expose the same xAPI over HTTPS. This driver covers the controls an AV integrator actually wires to a touch panel: standby on / off, volume, mute, dial, hangup, do-not-disturb, presentation start / stop, camera presets, and on-screen messages. xConfiguration writes are intentionally NOT included — settings belong in the Cisco web UI at install time, not on a control surface where they can be changed by accident.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the codec. 2. In the codec's web UI (https://<codec-ip>) go to Users and create
   (or note) a local user with at least the "Integrator" role. The
   default "admin" user works too. This driver uses HTTP Basic auth —
   SSO / single-sign-on users will not work.
3. Confirm xAPI over HTTPS is enabled. In the web UI: Settings ->
   Configurations -> NetworkServices -> HTTP Mode. Default is
   HTTP+HTTPS, which is fine. (HTTP-only is also supported by toggling
   the Use HTTPS field on this device.)
4. Add the codec in OpenAVC: enter the IP, leave port 443 / HTTPS on,
   enter the username and password from step 2.
5. Polling refreshes system info, standby, audio, DND, presentation,
   and people-presence every 30 seconds. Adjust the Poll Interval if
   you want faster touch-panel feedback.

compatible_models.notes: All models share the same RoomOS xAPI surface; one driver covers the whole family. Verified against the xAPI documentation; no live-hardware verification yet. The xAPI has been stable across CE9 / RoomOS 10 / 11 / 12 — minor command additions but the core surface used here predates CE9.

drivers.name: QLab Show Control
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Figure 53's QLab show-control / playback software (macOS) over OSC. GO, STOP, PANIC, pause/resume/reset, and per-cue start/stop/load/preview by number or unique ID, plus select, playhead, level, arm, color, and load-at. Live feedback: current cue id/number/name, running state, and QLab version. OSC remote control is free in QLab 5. UDP or reliable TCP+SLIP transport.

help.overview: Controls QLab, Figure 53's macOS show-playback and show-control app, over OSC. Fire and stop cues, PANIC (fade everything out and stop), pause, resume, reset, select cues, move the playhead, and set per-cue level, arm, and color. The current cue (id, number, and name), whether anything is running, and the QLab version are reported back live. Remote control over OSC is a free feature in QLab 5, so no license is needed to drive it.
help.setup:
1. In QLab on the Mac: Workspace Settings > OSC. Turn on "Use OSC
   controls" and note the port (default 53000). Optionally set a passcode.
2. Enter the Mac's IP address as Host and the port (default 53000). 3. Leave Workspace ID blank to control the front-most workspace, or enter
   a specific workspace's unique ID to target it (QLab shows the ID in
   Workspace Settings > OSC). On a Mac running more than one workspace,
   targeting an explicit ID is recommended.
4. If the workspace has an OSC passcode, enter it as Passcode. Leave blank
   if none is set.
5. Transport: leave at UDP for normal use. Choose TCP for the most
   reliable feedback (large cue-list replies) — QLab accepts both on the
   same port.
help.connection: If commands do nothing, confirm "Use OSC controls" is enabled in QLab's Workspace Settings > OSC and that the port matches. A set passcode must be entered here or QLab will reject control messages.

compatible_models.notes: Validated against QLab 5.6.1 over both UDP and TCP: connect/passcode, GO/STOP/PANIC, cue start by number/ID, and live feedback (version, current cue id/number/name, running state). OSC remote control is a free feature in QLab 5 across all license tiers (Free, Audio, Video, Lighting).
Shares the same OSC address grammar as QLab 5; video-specific addresses differ. Not tested against real QLab 4 hardware.

drivers.name: Novastar H Series Video Wall Splicer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Novastar H series video wall splicers via UDP JSON commands. Covers layer operations, preset management, input switching, brightness, fade-to-black, freeze, volume, test patterns, screen color, OSD, and device management. Compatible with H2, H5, H9, H15, H20, and similar models using the H Series Control Protocol.

help.overview: Controls Novastar H series LED video wall splicers. These processors manage LED wall layouts, input routing, presets, and screen settings. Common in large-format LED installations including houses of worship, corporate lobbies, broadcast studios, and live event stages.
help.setup:
1. Connect the processor to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the processor's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 3. Enter the IP address and port 6000 (default) in the device config. 4. Device ID defaults to 0. If using multiple processors, set the
   device_id config field to match each unit's ID.
5. Screen ID defaults to 0. Set screen_id for multi-screen setups.

drivers.name: Poly Studio (VideoOS)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Poly (HP) Studio X30, X50, X70, E70, and G7500 video collaboration bars via the public VideoOS REST API. Audio / video mute, volume, camera presets and direction nudges, hangup, reboot — everything needed to wire Poly bars into a touch panel.

help.overview: Poly VideoOS exposes a documented REST API on HTTPS 443 for control of audio mute, volume, privacy / video mute, camera control and presets, active call hangup, and system reboot. The driver uses session-cookie authentication — log in once with the device's admin credentials and the session is reused for the lifetime of the connection.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Poly bar to the network and assign a static IP.
2. From the bar's web UI (https://<ip>) sign in as Admin and confirm the API is enabled. The factory default password is the device's serial number on first boot — change it immediately to a site-specific password.
3. In OpenAVC, enter the bar's IP, the admin username (default ``admin``), and the password. Leave the port at 443.

compatible_models.notes: VideoOS REST API is identical across the X-series and G7500. Per-model differences (mic count, integrated cameras, bundled mic pods) don't change the command surface — they just gate which features actually do anything when invoked.

drivers.name: vMix
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls vMix video production software via the TCP API. Supports transitions, input switching, audio, overlays, recording, streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ.

help.overview: Full control of vMix video production software. Supports input switching, transitions, audio mixing, overlays, recording/streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ cameras.
help.setup:
1. Open vMix and go to Settings > Web Controller
2. Ensure the TCP API is enabled (default port 8099)
3. Enter the vMix PC's IP address and port below
4. Tally subscription is enabled by default for real-time program/preview tracking

compatible_models.notes: Any vMix edition. Requires TCP API enabled in vMix settings.

drivers.name: tvONE CORIOmaster
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls tvONE CORIOmaster, CORIOmaster mini/micro, and CORIOmaster2 video wall processors over the CORIOmax command-line API (TCP 10001). Windows, canvases, and the installed input/output cards are discovered from the unit and modeled as child entities — route sources into wall windows, move and resize windows, recall presets and storyboards, run canvas audio, and drive the Streaming Media card's playback, with live updates over the unit's event subscription.

help.overview: CORIOmaster is tvONE's modular video wall processor — slots take DVI, HDMI, SDI, HDBaseT, and Streaming Media cards, and outputs are composed into canvases carrying movable source windows. The driver logs in, discovers the installed cards, windows, and canvases, and models each as a child entity: windows carry their source and geometry, canvases their audio and active storyboard, outputs their cut-to-black state, inputs their signal status. Wall presets and storyboards recall from live dropdowns, and Streaming Media inputs expose playback transport controls. State updates arrive live through the unit's event subscription; polling covers older firmware.
help.setup:
1. Give the unit a static IP (default 192.168.0.10) and add it here with port 10001.
2. Enter the control login — the factory account is username admin, password adminpw (the password field is left blank on purpose; type the unit's real password).
3. The unit accepts one controller at a time: close any open CORIOgrapher / CORIOdiscover session first.
4. Build walls, windows, and presets in CORIOgrapher first; this driver operates what commissioning created. Use Refresh from Device after changing the configuration.
5. Keep polling enabled: the session logs out after a few minutes idle, and polling doubles as the keep-alive.

compatible_models.notes: All frames speak the same CORIOmax command-line API (CORIOmaster document v411.0.1, CORIOmaster2 document v503.0.1). Live event updates need firmware with the AddEvents mechanism (M411 / G503 documents); older firmware falls back to polling automatically. The unit accepts ONE controlling connection at a time — close CORIOgrapher before connecting OpenAVC. Standby mode is supported on the CORIOmaster micro only. Factory login is admin / adminpw.
